en: One of my camera traps caught a panda less than an hour ago! :[name=Researcher;face=40,dp_scientist_f-2x,255]:
She was heading north-west, toward the big mossy boulder. She looked very tired.:[name=Researcher;face=40,dp_scientist_f-2x,255]:
:[name=Ranger;face=40,dp_40-2x,255]:Pandas feed as they walk, so they leave chewed-down bamboo behind them.
:[name=Ranger;face=40,dp_40-2x,255]:Look for stalks bitten off at the base. They mark the path she took.
:[name=Ranger;face=40,dp_40-2x,255]:Mind the wildlife, too. Boars, bamboo rats and pit vipers all live in here.
:[name=Bamboo Cutter;face=60,dp_10-2x,255]:Those are boar tracks, not panda tracks. Count the toes: just two!
:[name=Bamboo Cutter;face=60,dp_10-2x,255]:If you're after the panda, go back out and take the eastern trail.
:[name=Farmer;face=100,dp_70-2x]:A panda? Something black and white crossed my field at dawn!
:[name=Farmer;face=100,dp_70-2x]:It went into the bamboo by the eastern trail, near the grey rock.
:[name=Farmer;face=100,dp_70-2x]:Not the western trail! That's where the wild boars wallow in the mud.
:[name=Keeper;face=100,dp_60-2x]:I'm so sorry! The old latch rusted through and the gate fell flat.
:[name=Keeper;face=100,dp_60-2x]:Look, her paw prints go straight out across the field, toward the bamboo.
:[name=Keeper;face=100,dp_60-2x]:Panda prints show five toes and a wide, round heel pad.
